feed.title: Common Shade: Signals
feed.subtitle: Which way heat policy, finance, research and practice are moving in South and Southeast Asia: what was announced, found or agreed, what the evidence confirms for each promise, and what would show the next step.

entry.title: 59 Belém Adaptation Indicators to measure progress on adaptation
entry.summary: At the 2025 UN climate conference (CMA 7), countries adopted a set of 59 Belém Adaptation Indicators to measure progress towards the targets for adaptation; reporting on them will serve as an input to the global stocktake. Who: Parties to the Paris Agreement (CMA 7). Where: Global (UN climate process). Latest development: 22 November 2026. Evidence states, sources and what is not known are on the record.

entry.title: COP31 lets the Adaptation Fund receive a share of carbon-market proceeds
entry.summary: Decisions at COP31 enable the Adaptation Fund to receive a share of the proceeds of carbon trading under the Paris Agreement's crediting mechanism. The decision is adopted; no money received under it, and none spent on heat, has been found yet. Who: Parties to the Paris Agreement (CMA 8). Where: Global (UN climate process). Latest development: 22 November 2026. Evidence states, sources and what is not known are on the record.

entry.title: Governments back a heat resilience and sustainable cooling roadmap at the Cooling Ministerial
entry.summary: At the third Cooling Pledge Ministerial in Antalya, co-chaired by Singapore and UNEP, governments backed a country-led, voluntary roadmap on heat resilience and sustainable cooling. More than US$20 million in new support was announced for the Cool Coalition's work on the Global Cooling Pledge. The roadmap is backed, not yet adopted, and the money is announced, not yet committed or paid out. Who: UNEP and the Government of Singapore (co-chairs). Where: Global (UN climate process). Latest development: 16 November 2026. Evidence states, sources and what is not known are on the record.

entry.title: COP31 opens in Antalya
entry.summary: COP31, the UN climate conference, is held in Antalya from 9 to 20 November 2026. Who: UNFCCC. Where: Global (UN climate process). Latest development: 9 November 2026. Evidence states, sources and what is not known are on the record.

entry.title: The Antalya Initiative for Health Resilience (AIR) launches on Health Day
entry.summary: COP31 opened with the launch of the Antalya Initiative for Health Resilience (AIR), a voluntary platform for countries to share their experience of making health systems resilient to climate risks. Health Policy Watch calls it the Antalya Initiative for Resilient Health Systems; this page uses WHO's name. On the launch day no country had yet announced that it would take part. Alongside it, a joint initiative with WHO brings climate information into public health planning: a forecast of dangerously high temperatures, for example, can help hospitals prepare for more patients. Who: Türkiye, as COP31 host, and the World Health Organization. Where: Global (UN climate process). Latest development: 9 November 2026. Evidence states, sources and what is not known are on the record.

entry.title: El Niño set to bring more heat into 2027
entry.summary: By mid-August 2026 El Niño had become firmly established. WMO's State of the Climate release says it has been intensifying since August and is expected to be the strongest on record by December. That is a forecast, not an observed record: NOAA's discussion of 12 November 2026 put the chance of a historic event (a three-month RONI of +2.5 °C or more) at about 60% for October to December 2026 and for November 2026 to January 2027. WMO calls El Niño a risk multiplier for health and writes that WHO has, for the first time, classified the anticipated health impacts as a health emergency. WHO's own plan describes a Grade 3 response, its internal grading of its operational response; no declaration of a public health emergency under the International Health Regulations was found. Who: World Meteorological Organization. Where: Global. Latest development: 9 November 2026. Evidence states, sources and what is not known are on the record.

entry.title: 2026 will be one of the four warmest years on record
entry.summary: WMO's State of the Climate Update 2026, released as COP31 opened, finds that the past 12 years have each been the warmest on record and the past four the top four. The global average surface temperature for January to September 2026 was about 1.47 °C above the pre-industrial average. In early November the EU's Copernicus service said 2026 is most likely to be the second-hottest year on record. It estimates that 146.5 million people in India were exposed to extreme heat in an April 2026 heatwave, and that the number of countries reporting multi-hazard early warning systems rose from 56 in 2015 to 136 in 2025. Who: World Meteorological Organization. Where: Global. Latest development: 9 November 2026. Evidence states, sources and what is not known are on the record.

entry.title: WHO responds to El Niño's health risks at Grade 3
entry.summary: WHO is responding to El Niño's health risks at Grade 3 under a Strategic Preparedness and Response Plan for October 2026 to September 2027, and names heat among the risks it is preparing for. It is a plan for WHO's own response, published during COP31; it does not show what reaches clinics or households. Who: World Health Organization. Where: Global. Latest development: November 2026. Evidence states, sources and what is not known are on the record.

entry.title: The Antalya Compact for Energy Efficient Buildings opens for endorsement
entry.summary: Ahead of the conference, the COP31 Presidency launched the Antalya Compact for Energy Efficient Buildings, which aims for a 25% cut in the operational energy intensity of buildings worldwide by 2035, compared with 2020. Its actions include stronger energy codes, faster renovation and the electrification of heating and cooling. It covers buildings and energy as a whole, not heat alone; it bears on heat because cooler, more efficient buildings ease the indoor heat people live and work in, and the cost of cooling them. Who: COP31 Presidency. Where: Global (UN climate process). Latest development: 29 October 2026. Evidence states, sources and what is not known are on the record.

entry.title: The Philippines issues guidelines on heat stress at work and on compensation for heat illness
entry.summary: In October 2026 the Department of Labor and Employment issued a labour advisory setting out steps for employers as the heat index rises during El Niño and other periods of extreme heat, and a second advisory on when heat-related illness at work may be compensated. Who: Department of Labor and Employment, Philippines. Where: Philippines. Latest development: 27 October 2026. Evidence states, sources and what is not known are on the record.

entry.title: Support for the Southeast Asia Heat Health Hub's next stage
entry.summary: Announced on 8 October 2026: support for the next stage of the Global Heat Health Information Network's Southeast Asia Hub, including funding for heat-health work in Indonesia (Makassar and two more cities) and Thailand in 2027, and preparations for a second Southeast Asia Heat Health Forum. The amount was not disclosed. Who: Philanthropy Asia Alliance. Where: Indonesia and Thailand. Latest development: 8 October 2026. Evidence states, sources and what is not known are on the record.

entry.title: The first Global Heat Forum, in Bangkok
entry.summary: Nearly 600 scientists, business leaders, philanthropists and health experts met in Bangkok from 6 to 9 October 2026. The Forum released the first country-level heat and health assessments for Bangladesh, Bhutan, India and Nepal, and a roadmap for investment and action on extreme heat. Who: Global Heat Forum. Where: Bangkok, Thailand (a global forum). Latest development: 6 October 2026. Evidence states, sources and what is not known are on the record.

entry.title: Only 35% of countries report health early warning systems for heat-related illness
entry.summary: IFRC's call to action for COP31 notes that only 35% of countries have reported having health early warning systems for heat-related illness. It asks for investment in multi-sector local action for cities and communities to reduce heat risk, from heat action plans and early warning to shock-responsive social protection and nature-based solutions. Who: International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies. Where: Global. Latest development: October 2026. Evidence states, sources and what is not known are on the record.

entry.title: 98% of surveyed maternity and newborn clinicians say they have cared for a pregnant woman they believe heat harmed
entry.summary: A survey commissioned by Wellcome asked 1,000 practising clinicians in pregnancy, childbirth, postnatal and newborn care, 250 of them midwives, in Australia, Brazil, India, the UK and Zimbabwe (fieldwork by Censuswide, September 2026). Across the five countries, 98% said they had cared for a pregnant woman, and 99% for a baby, whose health they believed extreme heat had harmed; 73% reported more heat-related complications in pregnant women over the past five years and 76% in foetal or newborn health, and 92% want more training and resources. As reported by Down To Earth, among the 200 respondents in India, 62% reported more complications in pregnant women and 66% in foetal or newborn health, and 26% had seen pregnancy complications that needed extra monitoring or treatment. The findings were presented on 13 November on the sidelines of COP31 in Antalya, where a UN Climate Change official said that about 1% of formal climate finance goes to health. These are clinicians' reports of what they believe they have seen, not measured outcomes. What clinicians in India can already use: on 6 May 2026 the health ministry and UNFPA India published guidance on heat and pregnancy for healthcare providers and community health workers, with a heat-risk checklist, preparedness for health facilities including functional referral systems, and counselling that covers breastfeeding. Who: Wellcome (commissioned the survey). Where: Australia, Brazil, India, the UK and Zimbabwe. Latest development: September 2026. Evidence states, sources and what is not known are on the record.

entry.title: Singapore makes heat stress measures mandatory for outdoor work from 1 December 2026
entry.summary: The Ministry of Manpower announced on 28 August 2026 that enhanced heat stress measures, including drinking water, become mandatory for outdoor work from 1 December 2026, giving employers three months to prepare. Measures that had been recommended become requirements. Who: Ministry of Manpower, Singapore. Where: Singapore. Latest development: 28 August 2026. Evidence states, sources and what is not known are on the record.

entry.title: India adds heatwaves to its notified natural calamities
entry.summary: In August 2026 India added heatwaves to its notified natural calamities, so national and state disaster response funds can pay for heatwave relief. Before, states could spend only up to 10% of their response fund on locally declared disasters such as heat. Heat mitigation projects are funded separately, from disaster mitigation funds. Who: Government of India. Where: India. Latest development: August 2026. Evidence states, sources and what is not known are on the record.

entry.title: World Bank: extreme heat already costs jobs and growth in South Asia's cities
entry.summary: The World Bank's report A Livable Future, published on 29 July 2026, finds extreme heat emerging as a major threat to jobs, productivity and growth across South Asia, and sets out how cities can protect them. Who: World Bank. Where: South Asia. Latest development: 29 July 2026. Evidence states, sources and what is not known are on the record.

entry.title: Bengaluru's city corporations announce first heat resilience money
entry.summary: At the launch of the Bengaluru Heat Collective on 15 July 2026, Bengaluru North City Corporation described ₹5 crore allocated for heat resilience by an NIUA pilot under AMRUT 2.0, ₹1 crore of it for vulnerable populations such as outdoor informal workers, and planned roof coating demonstrations on its buildings. Bengaluru South City Corporation announced ₹2 crore for phased implementation of the Begur Ward Climate Action Plan, called a starting point and not a final budget. The figures are reported by WRI India and others; no sanction order or spending record was found. Who: Bengaluru North City Corporation and Bengaluru South City Corporation (Greater Bengaluru Authority), with NIUA. Where: Bengaluru, India. Latest development: 15 July 2026. Evidence states, sources and what is not known are on the record.

entry.title: South Korea issues its first emergency heatwave warning under a new rating system
entry.summary: In July 2026 South Korea's weather service issued its first emergency heatwave warning, the top level of a new rating system, during a summer of record tropical nights. Workplaces added longer lunches and more breaks. Who: Korea Meteorological Administration. Where: South Korea. Latest development: 12 July 2026. Evidence states, sources and what is not known are on the record.

entry.title: Nearly all outdoor workers surveyed in Viet Nam's two largest cities report heat-related health problems
entry.summary: A 2026 study with UNDP surveyed 734 outdoor workers in Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City; 94% reported at least one heat-related health problem while working during heatwaves. Who: National Economics University with UNDP Viet Nam. Where: Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City, Viet Nam. Latest development: June 2026. Evidence states, sources and what is not known are on the record.

entry.title: April's pre-monsoon heatwave was made three times more likely
entry.summary: Fifteen days of heat in late April 2026 pushed India's electricity demand to a record and brought farm drought to more than a million square kilometres. Scientists found climate change made it three times more likely, and that April heat like this now returns about every five years. Who: World Weather Attribution. Where: India and South Asia. Latest development: May 2026. Evidence states, sources and what is not known are on the record.

entry.title: Bangladesh adopts its Health National Adaptation Plan
entry.summary: Bangladesh adopted its Health National Adaptation Plan 2026. It estimates about US$1.4 billion is needed over five years, and plans to draw on public budgets through a climate fiscal framework and on international climate funds such as the Adaptation Fund and the GCF. Who: Government of Bangladesh. Where: Bangladesh. Latest development: 31 March 2026. Evidence states, sources and what is not known are on the record.

entry.title: Singapore sets up a Heat Resilience Policy Office and funds heat research
entry.summary: In March 2026 a Heat Resilience Policy Office was set up to coordinate action across agencies, oversee research and draft a heat resilience action plan. A S$40 million 'Adapting to Heat Impacts' funding initiative supports research on heat impacts and community heat resilience. Who: Ministry of Sustainability and the Environment, Singapore. Where: Singapore. Latest development: March 2026. Evidence states, sources and what is not known are on the record.

entry.title: A South Asia climate-health desk and a heat research consortium
entry.summary: Announced on 20 February 2026: The Rockefeller Foundation and Wellcome fund a South Asia Climate-Health Desk under the WHO-WMO Climate and Health Joint Programme, and a South Asia Scientific Research Consortium, through a Rockefeller grant to IISER Pune, to develop tailored heat-risk thresholds. Amounts were not disclosed. Who: The Rockefeller Foundation and Wellcome. Where: South Asia. Latest development: 20 February 2026. Evidence states, sources and what is not known are on the record.

entry.title: Adaptation finance covers a fraction of what is needed
entry.summary: UNEP's Adaptation Gap Report 2026 estimates that developing countries need about US$305 billion a year for adaptation by 2035. International public adaptation finance to developing countries was about US$28 to 32 billion in 2024. Even if the COP30 aim of tripling it is met, it would cover only about 20 to 29% of needs. The report covers adaptation as a whole, not heat alone; it bears on heat because heat plans draw on the same adaptation money. Who: UN Environment Programme. Where: Developing countries. Latest development: 2026. Evidence states, sources and what is not known are on the record.

entry.title: Bangkok's heat plan opens 304 cooling centres
entry.summary: For the 2026 hot season Bangkok opened 304 cooling centres in schools, health centres and district offices. The city's own Urban Heat Management Action Plan for 2026 has 22 indicators, and a 2026 financing strategy with UNDP costs it at about THB 146 million to set up and THB 10.8 million a year to run, noting that running costs are not always covered. Who: Bangkok Metropolitan Administration. Where: Bangkok, Thailand. Latest development: 2026. Evidence states, sources and what is not known are on the record.

entry.title: The presidency's health theme: Dynamic and Resilient Health Systems
entry.summary: The COP31 presidency's action agenda includes a theme on Dynamic and Resilient Health Systems, which prioritises health systems that can anticipate, respond to and recover from climate-related shocks through preparedness, surveillance and resilient infrastructure. Unlike many other themes, it carries no numerical target for 2035. Who: COP31 presidency. Where: Global (UN climate process). Latest development: 2026. Evidence states, sources and what is not known are on the record.

entry.title: Warming will overshoot 1.5 °C: the Emissions Gap Report 2026
entry.summary: UNEP's Emissions Gap Report 2026, The Point of Return, finds that with global temperature rise set to exceed 1.5 °C, urgent and stringent cuts are needed to minimise the size and length of the overshoot and return to 1.5 °C by the end of the century. If current policies continue, warming could reach 2.8 °C this century; if all national pledges are delivered, 2.6 °C. Who: UNEP, with PBL Netherlands Environmental Assessment Agency. Where: Global. Latest development: 2026. Evidence states, sources and what is not known are on the record.

entry.title: The Extreme Heat Risk Governance Framework is piloted in Cambodia, Barbados and Senegal
entry.summary: In 2026 the Extreme Heat Risk Governance Framework and Toolkit is being piloted in Barbados, Senegal and Cambodia, with financial support from the Climate Risk and Early Warning Systems (CREWS) initiative. The pilots test practical tools for multi-sector coordination, financing and anticipatory action. Who: World Meteorological Organization and partners. Where: Barbados, Senegal and Cambodia. Latest development: 2026. Evidence states, sources and what is not known are on the record.

entry.title: Maharashtra sets up a Centre of Excellence for heat resilience and sustainable cooling
entry.summary: Maharashtra has set up a Centre of Excellence for Heat Resilience and Sustainable Cooling (CEHSC). The state disaster management authority's own site describes it as hosted within the Relief and Rehabilitation Department, and NRDC's 2026 review reports that it is to sit within the planned State Institute of Disaster Management. Who: Government of Maharashtra (Relief and Rehabilitation Department; Maharashtra State Disaster Management Authority). Where: Maharashtra, India. Latest development: 2026. Evidence states, sources and what is not known are on the record.

entry.title: India's Heat Resilient Cities Framework
entry.summary: India's National Institute of Urban Affairs published a Heat Resilient Cities Framework: a yearly city intervention plan, and a long-term heat resilience perspective. Who: National Institute of Urban Affairs, Climate Centre for Cities. Where: India. Latest development: 2026. Evidence states, sources and what is not known are on the record.

entry.title: Tamil Nadu and the UK set up a Heat Resilience Centre for the state
entry.summary: In November 2025 the Government of Tamil Nadu, with the Government of the United Kingdom, announced a Heat Resilience Centre for the state. The Tamil Nadu Green Climate Company runs it, with the British High Commission, UNEP and the World Resources Institute as partners. It is to act as a nodal institution for heat risk across sectors and to support heat action planning. Its programme was set to run until September 2026; whether it continues after that has not been verified. Who: Government of Tamil Nadu (Tamil Nadu Green Climate Company), with the UK Government. Where: Tamil Nadu, India. Latest development: November 2025. Evidence states, sources and what is not known are on the record.

entry.title: Bangladesh's first urban heatwave action plan, for Narayanganj
entry.summary: Narayanganj City Corporation's heat action plan was approved on 22 September 2025 and published in 2026. It gives each short-term action a tentative cost in taka and names potential funding sources, often development partners and NGOs. Who: Narayanganj City Corporation. Where: Narayanganj, Bangladesh. Latest development: 22 September 2025. Evidence states, sources and what is not known are on the record.
